Setup

Image upload & Send to Studio need a tiny Cloudflare Worker (Figma can't call Roblox directly — CORS). Deploy your own once, then paste its URL below.

  1. Open Cloudflare → Create Worker (free).
  2. Paste the worker code (worker.js) and Deploy.
  3. Copy the *.workers.dev URL here, then Test.
Studio Bridge
When enabled, the export is sent to Studio via the bridge instead of downloading a .rbxmx. In Studio, open the "Figma to Roblox" widget, enter the same Session Code and click "Pull from Figma".
Images
Enable this if you want any Images to be exported to Roblox
Enable this if you want control over an Image's Stroke within Roblox (otherwise the stroke will be applied into the image)
Fonts

Roblox can't upload fonts via the API, but it hosts most Google Fonts on the Creator Store. Find your font there, copy its asset id, and map it here — any text using that Figma family (e.g. Poppins) will then export with the exact typeface.

Help
Creating your Cloudflare Worker

Image upload and Send to Studio both require a small Cloudflare Worker — Figma plugin iframes are null-origin and cannot call Roblox APIs directly. You deploy your own Worker once (free tier is fine) and paste its URL into the plugin. Follow the steps below.

  1. Open Cloudflare → Workers & Pages → Create and choose Start with Hello World! (free).
  2. Give the Worker a name (this becomes your *.workers.dev URL) and click Deploy.
  3. Click Edit code — the editor opens. Delete the default Hello World code, paste the worker.js source below, then click Deploy again.
    worker.js — paste this into the Cloudflare editor 
    // Cloudflare Worker — CORS proxy for the Roblox Open Cloud Assets API.
//
// A Figma plugin runs in a null-origin sandbox, so calls to apis.roblox.com are
// blocked by CORS (the x-api-key header forces a preflight that Roblox does not
// answer). This Worker sits in between: the plugin calls the Worker, the Worker
// forwards the request server-to-server (no CORS there) to Roblox, and adds the
// CORS headers the browser requires on the way back.
//
// The plugin keeps sending its own x-api-key, so this Worker never stores any
// credentials — it is a transparent relay scoped to apis.roblox.com only.
//
// Deploy:
//   1. npm i -g wrangler   (or use the Cloudflare dashboard "Quick edit")
//   2. wrangler deploy     (from this proxy/ folder)
//   3. Copy the resulting https://<name>.<subdomain>.workers.dev URL into both
//      manifest.json (allowedDomains) and src/Converters.js (ROBLOX_ASSETS_API).

const ROBLOX_ORIGIN = "https://apis.roblox.com";

// Headers we relay from the plugin to Roblox.
const FORWARD_REQUEST_HEADERS = ["x-api-key", "content-type"];

// Bridge: how long a stored export survives if Studio never picks it up (seconds).
const BRIDGE_TTL_SECONDS = 3600;

function CorsHeaders() {
    return {
        "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
        "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "GET, POST, OPTIONS",
        "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "x-api-key, content-type",
        "Access-Control-Max-Age": "86400",
    };
}

function JsonResponse(Data, Status) {
    return new Response(JSON.stringify(Data), {
        status: Status,
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", ...CorsHeaders() },
    });
}

// Figma <-> Studio handoff over the Worker.
//   POST /bridge/:code  — Figma stores an .rbxmx payload keyed by a session code.
//   GET  /bridge/:code  — Studio polls and retrieves it; by default the entry is
//                         cleared on read so the same export isn't inserted twice.
//                         Pass ?peek=1 to read without clearing.
async function HandleBridge(request, env, Code) {
    if (!env.BRIDGE) {
        return JsonResponse({ error: "Bridge KV namespace not bound" }, 500);
    }
    if (!Code) {
        return JsonResponse({ error: "Missing session code" }, 400);
    }

    if (request.method === "POST") {
        const Body = await request.text();
        if (!Body) {
            return JsonResponse({ error: "Empty body" }, 400);
        }
        await env.BRIDGE.put(Code, Body, { expirationTtl: BRIDGE_TTL_SECONDS });
        return JsonResponse({ ok: true, code: Code }, 200);
    }

    if (request.method === "GET") {
        const Stored = await env.BRIDGE.get(Code);
        if (Stored === null) {
            return JsonResponse({ pending: true }, 404);
        }
        const Url = new URL(request.url);
        if (Url.searchParams.get("peek") !== "1") {
            await env.BRIDGE.delete(Code);
        }
        return new Response(Stored, {
            status: 200,
            headers: { "Content-Type": "application/xml", ...CorsHeaders() },
        });
    }

    return JsonResponse({ error: "Method not allowed" }, 405);
}

export default {
    async fetch(request, env) {
        // Preflight — answer it ourselves so the browser lets the real request through.
        if (request.method === "OPTIONS") {
            return new Response(null, { status: 204, headers: CorsHeaders() });
        }

        const Incoming = new URL(request.url);

        // Health check — used by the plugin's "Test worker" button.
        if (Incoming.pathname === "/ping") {
            return JsonResponse({ ok: true }, 200);
        }

        // Bridge endpoints are handled locally (KV), not forwarded to Roblox.
        if (Incoming.pathname.startsWith("/bridge/")) {
            const Code = decodeURIComponent(Incoming.pathname.slice("/bridge/".length));
            return HandleBridge(request, env, Code);
        }

        // Forward the exact path + query (e.g. /assets/v1/assets) to Roblox.
        const Target = ROBLOX_ORIGIN + Incoming.pathname + Incoming.search;

        const ForwardHeaders = new Headers();
        for (const Name of FORWARD_REQUEST_HEADERS) {
            const Value = request.headers.get(Name);
            if (Value) ForwardHeaders.set(Name, Value);
        }

        // Read the body fully so multipart uploads forward reliably.
        const Body = request.method === "GET" || request.method === "HEAD"
            ? undefined
            : await request.arrayBuffer();

        let RobloxResponse;
        try {
            RobloxResponse = await fetch(Target, {
                method: request.method,
                headers: ForwardHeaders,
                body: Body,
            });
        } catch (e) {
            return new Response(
                JSON.stringify({ proxyError: true, message: String(e) }),
                { status: 502, headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", ...CorsHeaders() } }
            );
        }

        // Relay Roblox's response, adding CORS headers.
        const ResponseHeaders = new Headers(RobloxResponse.headers);
        for (const [Key, Value] of Object.entries(CorsHeaders())) {
            ResponseHeaders.set(Key, Value);
        }

        return new Response(RobloxResponse.body, {
            status: RobloxResponse.status,
            statusText: RobloxResponse.statusText,
            headers: ResponseHeaders,
        });
    },
};
  4. For Send to Studio: in the Worker's Settings → Bindings, add a KV Namespace binding named exactly BRIDGE (create a new KV namespace if you don't have one already).

    The binding's Variable name must be exactly BRIDGE.

  5. Copy the *.workers.dev URL, paste it into the plugin's Worker URL field (and into the Studio plugin), then click Test.
Using the plugin

Select one or more frames in Figma, optionally tag elements using the toolbar on the left, then click Convert Selection. The plugin exports an .rbxmx file (or sends it straight to Studio if the bridge is enabled).

1. Select elements

Click a frame or group in Figma to select it. Multiple selections are supported.

2. Configure Image Upload (optional)

In the Images panel, enter your Cloud API Key, User/Group Id, and toggle Upload Images to have images automatically uploaded to Roblox during export.

  • Create an API key: Roblox → Open Cloud API Keys — add the asset permission (Read & Write).
  • Find your User Id (or Group Id): Creator Dashboard.
3. Send to Studio

Enable Send to Studio in the Studio Bridge panel, enter a Session Code, then in the Roblox Studio plugin paste the same Worker URL and Session Code and click Pull from Figma.

4. Tag them

Use the tag buttons (IMAGE, BUTTON, IMG BTN, FRAME, TEXT, SCROLL, ANCHOR, BG) in the left panel to mark nodes. Tags control how each element is converted — e.g. IMAGE → ImageLabel, BUTTON → TextButton/ImageButton, IMG BTN → ImageButton, FRAME → plain Frame, TEXT → native TextLabel (never turned into an image), SCROLL → ScrollingFrame. Tags are not case-sensitive and their short alt-names (IMG, BTN, TXT, SCRL) are stripped from the exported name.

The class tags (IMAGE, BUTTON, IMG BTN, FRAME, TEXT, SCROLL) are mutually exclusive — picking one clears any other on that node. ANCHOR and BG are independent modifiers you can combine. Clicking a tag again removes it. To tag several layers at once, Ctrl/Cmd-click them in the tree first (or Shift-click a range), then click the tag. By default only the selected layers are tagged; tick “Also tag parent frame” if you also want the parent affected.

Flattening a group into one image (baking)

Some artwork should become a single image in Roblox — for example a stylised button whose label is part of the drawing, or an icon badge with text baked into it. Whether this happens depends on what the parent is:

  • A plain Frame with children is not flattened — every child comes across as its own separate Roblox element (text stays real text, icons stay real images). Use this when you want the pieces editable in Studio.
  • Tag the parent as IMAGE or IMG BTN to flatten it: the whole group — its background, text and child layers — is baked into one picture and uploaded as a single ImageLabel / ImageButton. Its children are not exported separately.

Rule of thumb: Frame parent → keeps its children · Image / Image Button parent → bakes everything into one image. So if a flattened element looks squashed or shows the wrong picture, check that you tagged the right parent (the group that holds the pieces), not just one child inside it. If you only want a single layer rasterised, tag that layer itself with IMAGE.

5. Convert

Click Convert Selection. The plugin will export an .rbxmx file (or send it to Studio if the bridge is enabled).

Selection tree

The left panel lists your selection as a tree. Each row shows how it will export (the coloured badge).

  • Click a row to pick it (it also highlights in the Figma canvas so you can see what you're working on). Ctrl/Cmd-click to pick several.
  • Double-click a row to rename it. If multiple rows are picked, they're all renamed to the same name.
  • Double-click the badge to focus (isolate) that node in Figma.
  • ↶ Undo / ↷ Redo (or Shift+Z / Shift+Y) revert your tag & rename changes. This only affects the plugin's changes — it won't disturb Figma's own history, selection or camera.
Preview

The centre panel renders your selection so you can check it before exporting. Coloured outlines mark special elements (Buttons, Images, Text, ScrollingFrames); Frames & Backgrounds appear as hatched panels behind their contents.

  • Alt + scroll to zoom, plain scroll to move up/down, Shift + scroll for left/right, middle-mouse drag to pan. Double-click empty space resets the view. Zooming in re-renders in higher resolution so it stays sharp.
  • Hover an outline to see its name; left-click to pick that element (it lights up here and in the tree). Right-click for options such as Isolate in Figma.
  • Toggle Overlays in the header to show/hide the outlines. Use Hide panel to give the preview more room, and drag the bottom-right corner to resize the whole window.
Tags & Modifiers reference

You can often find more detailed information on GitHub.

Tags are not case sensitive. Alternative names (alt tags) are removed from name on export

Supported Tags (class — only one per node):
  • Image (alt: IMG) → ImageLabel
  • Button (alt: BTN) → TextButton / ImageButton
  • Image Button (IMGBTN) → ImageButton
  • Frame (|FRAME) → force a plain Frame (won't be rasterised to an image)
  • Scroll (alt: SCRL) → ScrollingFrame
Supported Modifiers (can be combined):
  • |ANCHOR - Enable AnchorPoint
  • BG / name 'Background' - donate this element's look to its parent group/frame

Tick “Also tag parent frame” to apply the same tag to a node and its parent group at once (useful for linking a TextLabel/Button to its background). It's off by default, so tagging a child never changes the parent on its own.

Frames with Auto Layout enabled automatically export as a ScrollingFrame.
